ownership.quote: Scaleway (formerly Online SAS or Online.net) is a French cloud computing and web hosting company, founded by Xavier Niel in 1999 and a majority owned subsidiary of the Iliad group.

stage.quote: a majority owned subsidiary of the Iliad group
stage.note: Scaleway is a wholly/majority-owned cloud division of the publicly traded Iliad Group (Euronext Paris: ILD), not an independently funded startup; it has not raised its own external VC rounds. Capital for large investments (e.g. its 2024 Nvidia H100 supercomputer purchase) comes from parent-company funding, not priced VC rounds.

note: Scaleway is not an independent startup: it is the cloud-computing division of France's Iliad Group (telecom operator Free's parent, controlled by billionaire Xavier Niel), originally launched as 'Online.net'/'Online SAS' in 1999-2000 and rebranded Scaleway in 2015. It funds large infrastructure investments (e.g. its 2024 purchase of an Nvidia H100-based supercomputer for AI/GPU offerings, and hosting the Iliad-backed open-source AI lab Kyutai) via parent-company capital rather than independent VC rounds, so classic funding-stage/round metrics (seed, Series A, etc.) do not apply. No standalone, current revenue figure for Scaleway was found within the research budget; Iliad Group as a whole is a large public company (Euronext Paris: ILD) with multi-billion-euro consolidated revenue, but that figure covers telecom (Free, Play, iliad Italia) as well as Scaleway and is not broken out per-segment in the sources reviewed.
